view: This print is one number: Q3 YARTEMLEA net sales, the first full quarter after a 3x quarter, against a bar that runs from about $31M (stale-ish Zacks-type) to $38M (updated aggregator), with the buy side probably near the top of that. My own arithmetic says a flat June run-rate already gets close to $35M: ordering accounts more than doubled during Q2 and ordering frequency rose, so June exited above the $9.5M Q2 monthly average, and Q3 added the permanent J-code from July 1. Management said on 2026-10-16, after the quarter, that it was ending the EU compassionate-use programme because of 'rising U.S. commercial demand for drug supply', which is the only post-quarter demand trace I found and it points up. Against that: no in-quarter data (no IQVIA, no conference remarks, no quarter-to-date number), Medicare NTAP only starts Oct 1, so some inpatient Medicare use may have waited, the company again gave no guidance, and the higher published consensus ($38M) already assumes about 33% growth. A 16-17% short float and a long-leaning options book make a beat move the stock more than a miss, but the call skew shows that asymmetry is partly paid for. Net: a modest lean up and no edge I can prove the price lacks.

recommendation.reason: The upward lean rests on launch arithmetic (exit rate from Q2, the J-code, the 73 accounts) and one post-quarter remark about rising US demand. I cannot show that the buy-side bar sits below what those imply: published consensus ranges from $31M to $38M and calls are already bid. Without any in-quarter sales data, I am below the 65% threshold.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 net YARTEMLEA sales at or below about $33M (flat to low growth on Q2's $28.5M), or a rise in distributor inventory above the 1.5 weeks of supply, would make this a clear down reaction. Net sales above about $42M with growth in reordering accounts would make it a clear up reaction.

self_critique: The case for up is almost all arithmetic that every analyst can do, and the $38M aggregator consensus suggests the street already models strong growth. The buy-side whisper after a 3x quarter may be $40M or more. In that case a merely good quarter (about $36-38M) could sell off like the -7.7% Q1 reaction, especially with the stock 19% off its high and the EU story broken. The 'rising US demand' line was said in a combative statement against the EMA and may be rhetoric. These points keep me near 50, not on a side.
approach_notes: P4 helped: the published consensus differed by $7M between sources, which turned 'beat likely' into 'bar unknown'. P3's freshest-data-first found almost nothing for a hospital-administered launch drug with no public script data. For this class of name the playbook could say plainly that, without in-quarter data, launch arithmetic alone rarely justifies a call.
